block.prompt:
SPEAKING — in pairs.

Tell your partner how you and your family usually pay for things (cash, card, phone, app…), when you last used real coins or notes, and how you would feel if cash disappeared completely. Ask your partner questions too — this is a conversation, not two speeches.

After you have talked, note down TWO ways in which your habits or feelings are DIFFERENT from your partner's.
block.answer_key: No single correct answer — this is a fluency and information-exchange warm-up. A strong pair talks in turns, asks follow-up questions (“Why?”, “Really? I always…”), and can then name two genuine differences (e.g. “I pay with my phone but she still uses cash for small things”; “I'd feel fine without cash, he'd feel worried”). Sample useful language: “I hardly ever carry cash these days.” / “The last time I used coins was probably at the bakery.”
block.acceptable_reasoning: Bewertet werden Redefluss, echtes Nachfragen und der Informationsaustausch — nicht der Inhalt der Zahlungsgewohnheiten. Die zwei notierten Unterschiede belegen, dass wirklich zugehört wurde.
watch_outs: Typischer Fehler: zwei parallele Mini-Monologe ohne Nachfragen. Vorab modellieren, wie eine Rückfrage klingt (‚Why do you prefer that?').
Manche verstummen nach zwei Sätzen — die Leitfrage ‚how would you feel if cash disappeared?' als Sprech-Motor bereithalten.
Auf einfache, aber korrekte Zeitformen achten: last used (Simple Past) vs. usually pay (Simple Present).

subject: Lebende Fremdsprache
kompetenzbereich: An Gesprächen teilnehmen und zusammenhängendes Sprechen
